script.title: A National Wealth Number Is Not Everyone's Paycheck
script.description: A historical Q2 2026 balance-sheet explanation distinguishing wealth totals from income and the distribution of gains.
script.topic: A National Wealth Number Is Not Everyone's Paycheck
script.why_us: US-focused educational explanation from reviewed primary sources.
script.timely_basis: Dated historical evidence or evergreen explanation; no claim of a current trend.

scenes.narration: America's one hundred ninety-five point nine trillion dollars in household and nonprofit net worth was not cash, in quarter two of twenty twenty-six.
The key calculation subtracts liabilities from assets; a wealth total is not an income or paycheck measure.
Owner-occupied real estate accounted for forty-nine point eight trillion dollars in that same quarter, within the household and nonprofit balance sheet.
Cash deposits appear alongside property and investments, so a balance sheet includes much more than spending money.
In quarter two of twenty twenty-six, households and nonprofits held two hundred seventeen point eight trillion dollars in assets against twenty-one point nine trillion dollars in liabilities.
A national balance sheet combines many owners, rather than describing one ordinary household.
Changes in asset values can change wealth totals without distributing identical gains to every household.

sources.title: Reviewed primary-source evidence
sources.content:
Table 1: Condensed household balance sheet
Trillions of dollars
| | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026:Q1 | 2026:Q2 |
| Assets | 162.8 | 175.9 | 189.5 | 203.8 | 204.7 | 217.8 |
| Owner-occupied real estate | 41.9 | 44.7 | 46.9 | 47.9 | 48.7 | 49.8 |
| Liabilities | 19.7 | 20.3 | 20.8 | 21.5 | 21.6 | 21.9 |
| Net worth | 143.1 | 155.7 | 168.7 | 182.3 | 183.1 | 195.9 |
Source: Financial Accounts of the United States, September 11, 2026.
The net worth of households and nonprofit organizations is assets minus liabilities. Assets include deposits, real estate and investments. Ownership is not evenly distributed. These are historical figures through June 30, 2026, not current balances. Changes in household net worth can reflect transactions and revaluations of existing assets, including equity and real estate. Because ownership is concentrated, households are not affected equally.

sources.title: Reviewed primary-source evidence
sources.content: Assets are what you own; liabilities are what you owe. Net worth equals assets minus liabilities. Assets can include savings, retirement plans, stocks, bonds and a home. A home value is an asset and its mortgage is a liability. Net worth is not the same thing as cash in an account.
